name: paper-plane

layers.notes: 13 pictures of the same plane banked from -36 to +36 degrees in steps of 6 (index = (bank + 36) / 6). Nose points UP in every picture.

motion.notes: Lazy chaotic flight in the background, no beam and no signals. wander.js is a small reference simulation (JavaScript, points and seconds): call step(dt) once per frame and read x, y (points from the centre of the figure), heading (radians, 0 = right, clockwise positive), bank (degrees), z (depth -1 far .. +1 near) and band (0..3, the layer). Port it to Swift as it is (about 50 lines). Picture: rotate by heading + pi/2. With k = 1 + par*z: position = centre + (x, (y - cy)) * k + (0, cy) with a vertical bob of 0.8 pt * sin(1.3 t); scale = base * (1 + kScale*z) * (1 + 0.04 sin(0.21 t)); opacity = alphaFar + (alphaNear - alphaFar) * (z + 1)/2. Recommended 'soft' depth: base 0.88, kScale 0.17, alphaFar 0.72, alphaNear 1.0, par 0.08. Stronger option: base 0.84, kScale 0.40, alphaFar 0.45, par 0.20, and a blur of 0.9 pt * (-z) when z < 0 (can be skipped). Frame: f = (bank + 36) / 6; draw frame floor(f) and dissolve frame floor(f)+1 over it with opacity f - floor(f). IMPORTANT: dissolve over an OPAQUE lower frame (or in an offscreen layer) and apply the plane's overall opacity to the result; two half-transparent frames drawn one over the other make the plane thinner for a moment, which looks like flicker.

trail.notes: Optional, very faint: remember the last 1.4 s of the tail position (11 pt * scale behind the centre, against the heading) together with the band it was made in; draw each piece in ITS band, as white segments with opacity (1-age)^1.6 * 0.30 * opacity and width (0.3 + 1.2 (1-age)) * scale, and every third sample a 0.8 pt spark with a random offset up to 3 pt. It can be dropped without loss.

on.notes: fade in over about 1.8 s, starting 0.4 s after the switch is turned on (after the figure lights up); fade out with the figure when it is turned off

draw_order: The plane has depth and is drawn in one of four layers, given by 'band' from the simulation: band 0 = before the back half of the halo (far behind everything); band 1 = after the back half of the halo, before the figure (behind the dog); band 2 = after the figure, before the front half of the halo (in front of the dog, inside the ring); band 3 = after the front half of the halo and the sparks (in front of everything). The soft glow of the stage is always below the plane. The simulation changes depth to the other side of the figure only while the plane is at least 82 pt to the side of the figure, so the layer never changes under the figure or the halo.
notes: Paper plane, 3D model rendered at 13 bank angles (python + numpy, own code). Canvas 64x64 pt (128x128 px), the plane is about 29 pt long at scale 1. Measured on the reference simulation (3 seeds, 30 minutes each, 60 fps): turns at most 104 deg/s, the bank changes by at most 0.8 degrees per frame, average speed about 17 pt/s, the layer changes about 4 times a minute, time is shared roughly evenly between the four layers (which one is more frequent depends on the seed), the layer under the figure is never changed closer than 82 pt to its middle. Files: 43 KB, memory 13 x 64 KB = 0.85 MB.
